complementarity.def: When one place has a supply of something that another place needs, so trade between them makes sense.

comparative-advantage.def: The ability to produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than another country: giving up less of other goods to make it. Trade follows comparative advantage.

absolute-advantage.def: The ability to produce more of a good than another country with the same resources.

neoliberalism.def: Policies that shrink the government's role in the economy: freer trade, lower tariffs, selling state-owned firms and cutting government spending.

trade-bloc.def: A group of countries that lower or remove tariffs and other trade barriers among themselves, such as the European Union or Mercosur.

tariff.def: A tax on imported goods. It raises their price, which protects a country's own producers.

imf.def: The International Monetary Fund: a body set up in 1944 that lends to governments in financial trouble, often on conditions such as spending cuts and open markets (structural adjustment).
